text:
Ottawa arrives at Buffalo having lost 6-3 at Anaheim three days ago, when the Ducks came back from three goals down and Cutter Gauthier scored three times. The Senators are 2-2-1 in their last five and closing a road trip, without William Eklund (ankle), Andre Burakovsky and Warren Foegele. In Eklund's absence, Tim Stützle has moved beside Dylan Cozens and Zetterlund, and Ridly Greig is up to 18:05 a night from 16:00. Buffalo has won three straight, though the chances only half back it: 51% of the expected goals, with goaltending doing extra work.

The teams are close in how they create and prevent chances. At five on five, Ottawa has taken 52% of the expected goals and Buffalo 51%. Our model has it nearly even tonight, 3.17 expected goals for Ottawa to 3.12 for Buffalo. The special-teams matchup to watch is Ottawa's power play (0.81 expected goals a game) against Buffalo's penalty kill (0.79 allowed), and the Senators take 5.1 penalties a game. In net, projected starter Samuel Ersson is at -2.0 goals saved above expected (how many goals he's stopped beyond what the shots called for) this season and -17.8 last year. Buffalo's projected starter, Colten Ellis, is at +1.1 and +2.2.

Watch Tage Thompson, our top pick to score for Buffalo at 39%, named the NHL's First Star of the Week. For Ottawa, Stützle (36% to score, 76% to get a point) skates with Cozens, Buffalo's former No. 7 pick. Drake Batherson carries a point streak into tonight, as CBS Sports noted.
